title: 2023 AMC 10A Problem 13
statement: Abdul and Chiang are standing \(48\) feet apart in a field. Bharat is standing in the same field as far from Abdul as possible so that the angle formed by his lines of sight to Abdul and Chiang measures \(60^\circ.\) What is the square of the distance (in feet) between Abdul and Bharat?

solutions.text: Let \(A\) be Abdul, \(C\) be Chiang with \(AC = 48,\) and \(B\) be Bharat with \(\angle B = 60^\circ.\) Every point seeing \(AC\) at \(60^\circ\) lies on one circular arc, so all valid \(B\) sit on a circle where chord \(AC\) subtends \(60^\circ.\) The law of sines gives its diameter, \(\frac{AC}{\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{48}{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}} = 32\sqrt3.\) Now \(AB\) is a chord, and a chord is longest when it’s a diameter. So \(AB = 32\sqrt3\) and \(AB^2 = 1024 \cdot 3 = 3072.\) Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Points that see segment \(AC\) at a fixed \(60^\circ\) lie on a circular arc through \(A\) and \(C\)
The farthest such point from Abdul is a diameter endpoint; find the circle’s diameter with the law of sines
